title: Claude Sheets: Anthropic's Spreadsheet, Limits and Pricing
desc: Claude Sheets launched in beta on November 10 in paid Claude plans, from $17 a month billed annually. A sheet holds up to 100,000 cells; no pivot tables yet.
keywords: claude sheets, anthropic sheets, claude spreadsheet, claude whiteboards, claude data, claude sheets limits, claude sheets pricing
cta: Want Claude connected to your team's workflows?
body:
November 11, 2026. Anthropic launched Claude Sheets in beta on November 10, 2026: a spreadsheet inside Claude that Claude builds and edits with you, with tabs, formulas, formatting, dropdowns and charts. Anthropic lists it in its paid plans, including Pro at $20 a month ($17 a month billed annually) and Team standard seats at $25 a month ($20 a month billed annually), with no separate price for Sheets; its use counts toward plan usage limits. A sheet holds up to 100,000 cells. Pivot tables are not available yet, macros are not supported, and sheets cannot pull live data from connected apps. Anthropic also launched Claude Whiteboards in beta and made Claude Data generally available.

What Anthropic launched

  1. Claude Sheets (beta). Anthropic's launch post says Claude "can now generate spreadsheets with tabs, formulas, formatting, and drop-downs, often from just a prompt like asking for a campaign tracker or a hiring budget." It edits in the cells, "outlining each new edit so you can track changes," and sheets can be shared with your team.
  2. Claude Whiteboards (beta). A shared board where your team brainstorms with Claude. In Anthropic's retro example, Claude groups everyone's notes by theme and drafts action items, and a board can be turned into a doc or deck or brought into tools such as Lucid and Miro.
  3. Claude Data (generally available). The renamed Claude Dashboards, which needs a data connector such as a warehouse or CRM. Certified queries and live sharing are in beta.
  4. Admin defaults. On Team plans all three are on by default. On Enterprise plans, Sheets and Whiteboards are off by default, and Claude Data "turns on by default on November 19, 2026." Anthropic says admins "can change these anytime in Organization settings > Artifacts."

Engadget reported that Anthropic announced Claude Sheets at an event in San Francisco, alongside Claude Meetings, a meeting agent that Engadget says is available in Google Meet to start and only to Team and Enterprise customers.

What Claude Sheets can and cannot do yet

Anthropic's help article lists 144 functions, conditional formatting, checkboxes, cell comments, version history, imports from CSV, Excel and Google Sheets, and export to .xlsx or CSV. Its current limits, from that article:

  1. "A sheet can hold up to 100,000 cells." That is about 10,000 rows by 10 columns.
  2. Not available yet: "Pivot tables, protected ranges, find and replace, multi-column sort, filter views, multi-select dropdowns, and PDF export."
  3. Excel features not supported: "Macros, VBA, Power Query, DAX, and print layout."
  4. Sheets "can't pull live data from connected apps," and docs, decks and dashboards cannot use a sheet as a data source.
  5. Web and desktop are supported, "with basic read-only access on mobile."
  6. HIPAA, CMEK and ZDR are "not yet supported."

What it means for operators

For a small team already paying for Claude, Sheets adds a shared tracker or budget without a new subscription. At Anthropic's list prices, five Team standard seats come to $1,200 a year billed annually, or $125 a month ($1,500 a year) billed monthly, with or without Sheets. Anthropic positions Sheets for "a light, shared sheet," and points to Claude for Excel or Claude for Google Workspace when a file already lives there or needs the full feature set. We would keep complex financial models and anything that needs macros in Excel or Google Sheets, keep health data out of Claude Sheets while HIPAA is not supported, and use Claude Sheets for drafts, campaign trackers and one-off analyses that get exported when they matter.

Enterprise admins have a date: Claude Data turns on by default on November 19, eight days after this article's date, so review the Artifacts settings before then. If a sheet is turning into a pipeline tracker, a tool from our sales automation software comparison may fit better, since Sheets cannot pull live CRM data. If you want Claude connected to your CRM and workflows, that is the kind of build our AI automation agency team takes on, and our AI search optimization service covers how a business appears in assistant answers.
faqs: Claude Sheets is a spreadsheet built into Claude that Anthropic launched in beta on November 10, 2026. Anthropic says you ask for a tracker, budget or model and Claude builds a working sheet that you, your team and Claude can edit together, with tabs, formulas, formatting, dropdowns and charts. Sheets export to .xlsx or CSV.
Which Claude plans include Claude Sheets?

Anthropic says Claude Sheets is in beta on the Pro, Max, Ultra, Team and Enterprise plans. It is on by default on Team plans and off by default on Enterprise plans until an admin turns it on in Organization settings under Artifacts. Anthropic lists it only for paid plans, its pricing page shows no separate price for it, and its use counts toward plan usage limits.
What are the limits of Claude Sheets?

A sheet holds up to 100,000 cells. Pivot tables, protected ranges, find and replace, multi-column sort, filter views, multi-select dropdowns and PDF export are not available yet. Macros, VBA, Power Query, DAX and print layout are not supported, sheets cannot pull live data from connected apps, and mobile access is basic and read-only.
Should I use Claude Sheets or Claude for Excel?

Anthropic suggests Claude Sheets for a light, shared sheet you build with Claude, and Claude for Excel or Claude for Google Workspace when the file already lives in those apps or you need their full feature set. You can also export a Claude sheet to .xlsx and continue in Excel.
